whenToUse: Light actions that almost always succeed, such as likes, bookmarks, or checks.
Waiting for the response makes it feel slow.
Actions that are easy to revert if they fail.
whenNotToUse: Actions that only mean something once confirmed, such as payments or transfers.
Actions whose values come back changed from the server (issuing an order number, for example).
Actions that fail often (constant reverting is more confusing).

alternatives.name: Spinner
alternatives.reason: People must wait until the result is confirmed.

alternatives.name: Undo
alternatives.reason: Applying first but giving people a chance to cancel themselves.

accessibility: The button's aria-pressed changes immediately, so screen readers read the new state at once.
If it fails, a role="status" message ("Couldn't save your like") explains why it reverted.
Don't convey failure only by the number going back.
With React 19's useOptimistic, the value settles naturally on the confirmed one when the request ends.
